Flag definitions

A flag marks a row where one specific, checkable condition holds. Only two of them move a number — DUE and REGRESSION nudge the Anytime TD composite. Every other flag is a label: it tells you what is unusual about the row and leaves the score alone. Chip colour follows what the backtest measured, not what the name suggests — WORKHORSE and ALPHA sound like positives and are not, so they are grey.

Anytime TD

DUE
Touchdowns are running well behind the chances taken: fewer than half the expected TDs (red-zone plus goal-line opportunities × 0.16) and at least 2 short, over 6+ games and 8+ opportunities. Adds a small bonus to the composite.
REGRESSION
The same comparison inverted: more than 1.9× the expected TDs and at least 2 clear. Subtracts from the composite — the conversion rate, not the role, has been doing the scoring.
GOAL LINE
0.9 or more goal-line opportunities per game. The most direct route to a touchdown there is.
SPOT
His team’s implied total is 27 points or more — the game script the market expects is a scoring one.
VOLUME
Opportunity score 72+ with an efficiency score of 45 or below: he gets the touches without doing much with them. Descriptive, not a recommendation.

Yards

Four markets, and one of them is not measured in yards. Receptions is a catch count: it prices off the same routes run as receiving yards, against a different rate — how often a route becomes a catch, which is targets per route times catch rate, both regressed. Read every market against its own column only, and note that the # column ranks within a market, so #1 is the top projection for that market rather than the biggest number on the board.

Every lean below is measured within a single market, as pooled actual over pooled prior-per-game for flagged players against unflagged ones — a 240-yard passing baseline cannot be weighed against a 25-yard receiving one. Re-derive them all with node fit_weights.js. Where three figures are given they are the 2023, 2024 and 2025 seasons in that order; a lean that changes sign between seasons does not replicate, and the entry says so.

SMASH SPOT
Environment multiplier 1.08 or better. Does not replicate across seasons. Rushing −11% / −6% / +11%, catches +1% / +9% / +3%, receiving yards +1% / +4% / +9% with only 2025 clear of zero. A description of the matchup, not an upward lean.
TOUGH DRAW
Environment multiplier 0.93 or worse. Does not replicate across seasons — the sign flips: receiving yards +3% / +11% / −17%, catches +5% / +5% / −11%, passing +32% / +19% / −7%. A description of the matchup, not a downward lean.
WIND
Weather score under 42 on a pass-sensitive market. Receiving yards −6% / −3% / −7% and passing −5% / −11% / −14%, the same sign every season. Catches (−2% / +5% / −7%) do not replicate.
DEEP THREAT
Average depth of target 12.0 yards or more. Receiving yards −5% / −4% / −12%: the same sign every season, but clear of zero only in 2025. Catches +7% / +11% / −1% flip sign and do not replicate — the old reading, that the boom-or-bust is in the yards and not the catch count, rested on 2025 alone.
WORKHORSE
Projected volume at or above the market’s cut (33 routes for either receiving market, 16 carries, 35 attempts). Not a positive lean — it marks the most predictable rows: error runs 41–47% of baseline against 63–70% elsewhere.
ALPHA
Target share 25% or more. Also a reliability marker, not an edge: error 44% of baseline against 70% elsewhere, and 35% against 58% on catches — the most predictable rows anywhere on this board.
YAC
55% or more of receiving yards come after the catch. Purely descriptive — no measurable lean either way (−0.8%). Deliberately absent from the receptions market: where his yards come from says nothing about how many balls he catches.
THIN SAMPLE
Model confidence under 0.55. The least reliable rows on the board: error 77% of baseline against 54% elsewhere.
NEW TEAM
Changed teams since last season. No lean that replicates: receiving yards −14% / +10% / −24%, catches −6% / +2% / −18%, on 84–96 mid-season movers a season. A caveat about where his usage was earned, not a direction.

Defense

EVERY DOWN
55+ snaps per game — he is on the field for the whole script.
RUSHER
0.6 sacks per game or more.
VOLUME
6 tackles per game or more.
SOFT FRONT
The opposing line allows a sack on more than 8.2% of dropbacks.

Games

MODEL LIKES HOME / AWAY
The model’s line differs from the market’s by 2.0 points or more. Named a disagreement rather than an edge on purpose: the backtest says this model loses to the market on the spread at every threshold, so the chip is deliberately uncoloured. Do not read it as a side.
LEAN OVER / LEAN UNDER
The model’s total differs from the market’s by 2.5 points or more.
WEATHER
Game weather score under 40.
NEUTRAL SITE
No home-field advantage applied.
DIVISION
A divisional game.

Any board

INJURY
Listed out or doubtful. Check the designation before using the row at all.
NO HISTORY
No prior-season usage to measure. His usage is a role estimate, not a measurement. With no depth-chart slot either, the touchdown score carries −20: such rows scored at about half the rate their score implied in every season 2023–25 (observed over expected 0.48 / 0.55 / 0.50).
